full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, the respondent No.2, filed a bankruptcy case being Bankruptcy case No.1 of 2000 in the Bankruptcy Court Additional District Judge Chittagong claiming Taka 7,23,89,000.00 if necessary by selling of the property belonging to the petitioner company by appointing a receiver. 

 6. Mr Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the Bankruptcy Act, 1997 is a special law which provides for rejection of the plaint under section 28 of the said Act but the learned judge in disposing of the petition filed on behalf of the petitioners, failed to reject the plaint of the Bankruptcy Case in exercise of its jurisdiction under sub-section 1(Ka) of section 28 of the said Act. He further submits that the learned Judge acted illegally in holding that the matters raised in the petition under section 28 of the Bankruptcy Act would be decided at the time of hearing of the Bankruptcy Case and would be dealt with after taking evidence in the case but the learned Advocate submits, section 28 enjoins upon the learned Judge to dispose of the petition after taking into consideration the relevant points as raised in the petition filed under the said provision but he failed to exercise his such jurisdiction under the said provision of law, consequently, the said order of rejecting the prayer for rejection of the plaint was illegal and without any lawful authority. 

 7. On the other hand, Mr Md Muzibur Rahman Miah, the learned. Advocated appearing on behalf of the respondent-bank, submit that bank, in accordance with the provisions of the Bankruptcy Act, 1997 presented the case after compliance of all the pre-conditions spelt out in the said provisions by issuing the notice demanding the payment and after the expiry of the requisite period as spelt out in the Bankruptcy Act filed the case. In that view of the matter, the learned Advocate submits, this petition under Article 102 is misconceived and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and also perused the petition and affidavit in-opposition and supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners and the respondent bank. It appears that after filing of the bankruptcy case on 24-1-2000 (Annexure-B) the defendant petitioners filed an application on 31-8-2000. (Annexure-I) under section 28 of the Bankruptcy Act (the Act, in short) praying for dismissal of the plaint. A written objection was filed on behalf of the respondent-bank on 24-3-2000 (Annexure-D) contending, inter alia, that in spite of issuance of notice under section 9(1)(Jha) of the Act asking them to repay the outstanding dues within the period of 90 days but without any response and since the dues of Taka 7,23,89,000 remained outstanding as on 30-12- 1996, the defendant committed an act of bankruptcy. 

 9. It appears that the learned Judge by his order No. 17 dated 7-11-00 after hearing of the said petition under section 28 of the Act found that the defendants failed to show that the plaintiff was not entitled to file the bankruptcy case or that the notice under section 22 (2) of the Act was not issued, or that the defendants did not commit any act of bankruptcy, that notice under section 9(1)(Jha) was not issued or that the defendants are able to repay the loan or they are not defaulters. The learned Judge further found that the contents of the petition for dismissal of the plaint are dependent on proof of allegations on evidence to be recorded at the time of hearing of the suit, as such, he rejected the said petition filed under section 28 of the Act praying for dismissal of the plaint. 

 13. In the instant case, it appears from the averments made in the plaint of the bankruptcy case that the respondent-Bank allowed loans to the defendant company and the defendant Nos. 2 to 9 guaranteed repayment of the said loans but the defendant company failed to repay which stood at Taka 7,23,89,000.00 as on 30-12-1996, as such, the plaintiff-bank issued a notice as envisaged under section 9 (1)(Jha) on 4-8-1998 giving them 90 days time to repay the said dues but when no response was received, this case was filed on 23-1-2000. Apparently, as stated in the plaint, the defendant- petitioners committed an act of bankruptcy. These facts are also stated in the written objection dated 24-9-2000 (Annexure-D) filed on behalf of the respondent-bank. On the other hand, in the petition filed on 31-8-2000 (Annexure-I) under section 28, it was not shown to the satisfaction of the Court that the defendants are able to repay their debts or that are not wilful defaulters or that there were any other cogent reason for which an order of adjudication should not be made. It is true that a statement was made in paragraph 4 of the petition that they are not wilful defaulters but the rest of the facts in support of such statements are contentious. It is true that in paragraph 7 it is stated that they had already repaid Taka 10,00,000 but since there is overwhelming amount of demand for more than Taka 7 crore, this payment of Taka 10,00,000, even if it is true, does not show that the defendant petitioners are able to repay the said huge amount of dues or they are not wilful defaulters. It appears that there are so many other facts in the said petition which are not the subject matter of section 28 and can only be resolved on taking evidence. Since from reading of the petition under section 28 dated 31-8-2000 and the plaint of the Bankruptcy case, it clearly appears that the respondent-bank satisfied the requirements of sub- section 1 (ka) of section 28, under such circumstance, the learned Judge of the Bankruptcy Court rightly rejected the petition leaving the parties to prove their own averments made in the plaint and the written statements and in the petition under section 28 of the Act for decision in the suit on taking evidence. Under the circumstances, we do not find any illegality in the decision in rejecting the said petition filed on behalf of the defendant petitioners. 

 14. It also appears that the defendant- petitioners had filed their written statement on 11-1-2001 and the hearing of the said Bankruptcy case had already been started on 28-2-2001, as such, the defendants are at liberty to raise all their objections before the Bankruptcy Court at the hearing of the main case. Case No.2 of 1998 (Annexure-F) under Article 33 of the President's Order No. 129 of 1972, praying for a decree for Taka 8,08,99,511 filed on 3-5-1998. In respect of the said Miscellaneous case, it is stated in paragraph 3 of the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent No. 2 on 17-4-2004 that the said Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 1998 had already been dismissed for non payment of advalorem Court fees. 

 15. Under such circumstances, this Rule is discharged but without any order as to costs. The learned Judge of the Bankruptcy Court is directed to dispose of the bankruptcy case expeditiously.
